messages.author: 9cfe4fa1955c99f3
messages.subject: Trouble running weighted ADKEs
parts:
Hi Chris, I'm hoping you can help me out with a couple of things.
The first: I have telemetry tracking data from sharks using high density arrays, that render positions accurate to a few meters, with positions every couple minutes or so.
If I run the animals individually, following the methods described in the paper, I can run ADKEs (weighted or not) without a problem.
However, when I follow the vignette to run them as a batch in parallel, it will not run the WAKDEs for my data. It will do it just fine for the example Buffalo data, but for my data, R never stops (at least after 2.5 days) trying to run it. The unweighted ADKE in parallel works just fine. Can you think of any reasons this may be?

The second issue: I'm trying to look at Conditional Distribution of Encounters.
the first attempt at using the cde function yielded the following response

`Error in cde(ADKES[c("2020-13","2020-15")]) : could not find function cde.

So i looked up the source code for the function, ran that separately, then tried again.
This time it returned the error: `Error in check.projection(UD) : could not find function "check.projection".
I also tried CDE<- stmm::cde(ADKES[c("2020-13","2020-15")], but got the error `Error: 'cde' is not an exported object from namespace:ctmm'

Again, any ideas or pointers would be greatly appreciated.
Cheers,

James

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Trouble running weighted ADKEs
parts:
Hi James,

If the individuals have ranges with vastly different scales, then you can run out of memory (or take forever calculating with virtual memory) trying to put everything on a high resolution grid. I recently added a dr.fn argument to the grid argument of akde() that you can quickly use to automate a coarser resolution like akde(...,grid=list(dr.fn=max)) which will take the maximum individual cell size, whereas the default will take the minimum individual cell size. Please see if that works.

Best,
Chris
